name: Joshua
summary: Israel's leader after Moses, a former spy known for his faith at Kadesh-barnea, commissioned by the LORD to bring Israel into Canaan. Joshua leads the conquest, divides the land among the tribes, and dies at a hundred and ten after renewing Israel's covenant at Shechem.

name: Rahab
summary: A prostitute living in Jericho's city wall who hides Israel's two spies and is spared with her family when the city falls, becoming part of Israel.

name: Achan
summary: An Israelite of the tribe of Judah who secretly keeps devoted plunder from Jericho, bringing Israel's defeat at Ai until his sin is exposed by lot and he is executed.

name: Caleb
summary: One of the twelve spies who gave a faithful report of Canaan forty-five years earlier; now eighty-five, he asks Joshua for the hill country of Hebron as his inheritance.

name: Eleazar
summary: The priest who, alongside Joshua, oversees the division of the land among the tribes by lot at Shiloh.

name: Phinehas
summary: Eleazar's son, who leads the delegation confronting the Transjordan tribes about the altar they build by the Jordan.

name: Othniel
summary: Caleb's younger relative who captures Kiriath-sepher and wins Caleb's daughter Achsah in marriage.

name: Achsah
summary: Caleb's daughter, given in marriage to Othniel after he captures Kiriath-sepher; she asks her father for springs of water to go with her inherited land.

name: The Two Spies
summary: The two unnamed men Joshua sends to scout Jericho, sheltered by Rahab and smuggled out of the city by a rope.

name: The People of Israel
summary: The assembled people of Israel, who set up a memorial of stones at Gilgal after crossing the Jordan and renew their covenant with the LORD at Shechem.

name: The Gibeonites
summary: The inhabitants of Gibeon, who disguise themselves as distant travelers to trick Israel into a peace treaty and are afterward made servants for the community's worship.

name: Zelophehad's Daughters
summary: The five daughters of the late Zelophehad, who receive a land inheritance in Manasseh's territory since their father died with no sons.

name: The Reubenites, Gadites, and Half-Tribe of Manasseh
summary: Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, already settled east of the Jordan, who send their armed men to help conquer Canaan before returning home and building a disputed altar.

name: Adoni-zedek
summary: The king of Jerusalem who leads a coalition of five Amorite kings against Gibeon and is captured and executed at Makkedah.

name: Jabin
summary: The king of Hazor who leads a large northern coalition against Israel at the waters of Merom; Israel defeats his army and burns his city.
